headline: Crypto deleverages into a Fear & Greed drop (69 to 57, z30 -1.8; HL OI $11.7B, z30 -1.5) while BTC holds $83.6K, 2.5% above the ETF cost basis that hl-cycles says would invalidate its risk-on read
tldr: Regime: hl-cycles mild risk-on (66% BTC, 2 days old; 1 of 6 stress conditions on). Main change: HL OI fell from $12.4B to $11.7B and alts bled (SOL -4%, HYPE -5%, ZEC -9% on 24h) while BTC was nearly flat (-0.4%); BTC dominance eased to 59.4% and no series is at |z30| >= 2. Main disagreement: equities sit near highs (S&P 7,807, VIX 15.2) and hl-cycles is risk-on, yet its Macro lens is Restrictive (34), the 10Y is 5.22% (Oct 8) and Brent was $125 on Oct 6 (FRED). Next catalysts: Sep CPI Oct 14, Russia/Iran sanctions deadline Oct 18, FOMC Oct 27-28. Not financial advice.

domains.summary: Yields are elevated and stable: 10Y 5.22% and 2Y 4.75% on Oct 8 (FRED, latest print; Oct 12 bond holiday), 2s10s +47bp (+44bp Oct 9), 30Y 5.60%. Brent was $125.44 and WTI $96.24 on Oct 6 (FRED; one news item put Brent near $102 on Oct 2 while FRED shows $135.51 that day, so we treat the level as low-confidence), the dollar index 121.38 on Oct 2 (up about 0.9% from Sep 25). The fed funds effective rate is 3.88% after the Sep 16 hike. Futures-implied odds of an October 27-28 hike fell to roughly 17-20% after a weak September jobs report (from about 64% on Sep 25), while about 80-85% is priced for at least one hike by December; one outlet's '50-50' headline conflicts with the others and is treated as stale. We read this as restrictive: oil above $100 keeps an inflation input alive, and September CPI on Oct 14 (single-source consensus about 3.7% headline, 2.4% core) is the swing print. A soft print with oil still high would argue the market is leaning on growth weakness; a hot one reopens October hike odds. hl-cycles Macro lens: 34 (Restrictive).

US cash session of Oct 12 (Yahoo/FRED): S&P 500 7,807.24 (-0.06%), Nasdaq 27,245.90 (-0.44%), Dow 51,850.55 (+0.38%); SPY +0.4% over 5 sessions, QQQ -1.3%, IWM -1.9% (small caps lagging). VIX 15.21 (+2.5% on the day, 14.84 on Oct 9), so the tape is calm. The read is a quiet index masking a rotation out of semis (SMH -6.8% over 5 sessions) into platforms. Calm VIX against a 5.2% 10Y is the part we would not rely on: a hot CPI print on Oct 14 is the nearest thing that could move volatility. No put/call ratio found.

Price/OI/funding: BTC -0.4% 24h ($83,651 HL mark) with OI down to $3.15B (z30 -1.6) and funding barely positive (+0.0010%/h, z30 +1.0) is mild deleveraging, not a press by either side. Alts did the selling: SOL -4.0%, HYPE -5.2%, ETH -1.4% with OI also lower (HL total $11.7B, z30 -1.5, from $12.4B). Fear & Greed dropped 12 points to 57 (z30 -1.8, closest reading to the |z| 2 line), and a fast sentiment drop alongside falling OI often marks a washout rather than fresh shorting. Crowding is low: funding skew z30 +0.7, no asset above z30 +1.0. BTC dominance 59.4% (z30 +0.9, no longer unusual) and the stablecoin supply is flat ($312.8B, -0.5% over 7d, +0.8% over 30d), so we read it as no new dry powder arriving. BTC is moving with SPY, not with Nasdaq/semis (QQQ -1.3% 5d vs BTC +0.4%), so it looks idiosyncratic rather than macro-driven (low-confidence). What would change the read: OI rebuilding with funding above z30 +2 would mean leverage is returning.

Oct 12 closes (Yahoo), with 5-session change: META $742.96 (+3.4% day, +0.1% 5d), AAPL $340.97 (+1.3%, +2.4%), MSFT $541.15 (+1.1%, +3.0%), GOOGL $352.72 (+0.3%, +1.8%), AMZN $259.53 (-1.1%, +3.2%), NVDA $226.32 (-1.3%, -5.3%). SMH $590.99 fell 2.1% on the day and 6.8% over 5 sessions. Dispersion is the story: platform and software names are holding or rising while the semis complex, led by NVDA (about 22% of SMH), is the weak spot, so breadth within AI is narrowing to the downside. What would change the read: NVDA reclaiming its 5-day losses with SMH stabilising would remove the semis-led stress. No earnings dates for the six were verified this run.

The Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act (signed Sep 18) calls for implementation by Oct 18, including tariffs of up to 100% on top importers of Russian energy (China and India named in reporting), with a broad national-interest waiver, so the president keeps discretion. Searches this run returned no implementation news dated this week, so the newest item we can cite is from late September. Linkage: with Brent at $125 on Oct 6 per FRED, an actual tariff on a top oil importer would plausibly add to the inflation input ahead of the Oct 27-28 FOMC; a waiver or delay would likely remove that risk. Hormuz and Iran-related reporting found was dated Sep 2 to Oct 2.

thesis.observe: BTC $83,651 (HL mark, -0.4% 24h); HL OI $11.7B (z30 -1.5), down from $12.4B; Fear & Greed 57 (z30 -1.8); BTC funding +0.0010%/h (z30 +1.0); no series at |z30| >= 2. hl-cycles: mild risk-on 2 days, Compass 48 (Neutral), Macro 34 (Restrictive), ETF cost basis $81.7K, True Market Mean $79.2K, STH cost basis $74.1K. S&P 7,807 (Oct 12), VIX 15.2, 10Y 5.22% (Oct 8), Brent $125.44 (Oct 6).
thesis.infer: Positioning: price flat, OI down, funding barely positive means longs and shorts are both trimming, with alts taking the damage; crowding is low. Disagreement: equities near highs and hl-cycles risk-on sit against a Restrictive macro lens, a 5.2% 10Y and oil above $100, a market holding up without leverage or new stablecoin supply. Consensus is pricing a low chance of an October hike but a December hike; we read September CPI as the test of that pricing.
thesis.forecast: Base case (we lean here, low-confidence): BTC chops between the ETF cost basis ($81.7K) and the mid-$80Ks while OI stays subdued into CPI. Tail case (low-confidence): a hot CPI or tariff shock sends a daily close below $81.7K, which hl-cycles lists as invalidating its read, and risk skews to a test of the True Market Mean ($79.2K, about 5.7% below). Second tail case (low-confidence): a soft CPI revives leverage, with OI back above $12.1B (its 30d mean) and funding z30 above +2 turning the rally fragile. Consensus is pricing a hold in October; we read the risk as sitting in the December path.
thesis.disclaimer: Not financial advice. Market intelligence only — a reasoned read of public data, not a recommendation to buy or sell anything.

risks: Daily BTC close below $81.7K (ETF cost basis, hl-cycles invalidation level)
September CPI (Oct 14) headline above the ~3.7% consensus
HL total OI rising back above $12.1B (30d mean) with BTC funding z30 above +2 (leverage returning, fragile rally)
SMH falling a further 5% over the next 5 sessions (semis stress spreading to the index)
